constraints: Use standard-library Python and preserve validate_claims(claims, now) -> bool; invalid inputs return False without raising.
Require dict claims and a string sub that is nonempty after stripping whitespace.
Require integer exp and now, explicitly excluding bool; reject strings, floats, NaN, and other types.
Allow exactly seven seconds of skew: now < exp + 7.
Never read the wall clock, add third-party dependencies, or mutate caller dictionaries.
acceptance: Implemented A.1 in expiry.py with deterministic validation and the public bool API.
Added tests covering malformed inputs, timestamp types and ranges, dictionary preservation, and the strict skew boundary.

decision.summary: Validate types and ranges before comparing now < exp + 7.
decision.rationale: Explicit checks reject malformed timestamps without coercion and preserve deterministic behavior.

failure.summary: F-001: Prior int(value) coercion accepted invalid timestamps.
failure.cause: Coercion accepted numeric strings and truncated fractional timestamps.

lesson.title: L-001: Explicitly exclude bool from integer timestamps
lesson.summary: Python bool subclasses int. Check isinstance(value, int) and explicitly reject isinstance(value, bool) before arithmetic.
lesson.applicability: Use this pattern whenever an integer-only API must reject booleans; validate types instead of coercing inputs.
